target.title: fix: preserve OpenAI Responses message boundaries
target.body:
Closes #106569.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users could lose OpenAI Responses message boundaries when two separate assistant message items are emitted in the same phase and the second message starts with the first message's text, such as `Hello` followed by `Hello world!`.

The previous collapse rule treated that pattern as a cumulative snapshot and replaced the first message block, corrupting transcript structure and stream lifecycle events.

## Why This Change Was Made

The snapshot collapse rule now requires the prior and next message to share the same normalized Responses item id or the same Responses `output_index`, plus the same phase, before replacing the prior text block. Distinct `output_index` values are treated as distinct output items, even when their text is prefix-related.

This preserves the existing compatibility path for providers that emit cumulative snapshots with rotating message ids on the same output slot, while preventing separate indexed Responses message items from being merged. The same lineage boundary is applied in both the shared Responses stream processor and the agent transport path.

## User Impact

OpenAI Responses chats preserve separate assistant message blocks when the provider emits multiple same-phase message items. Existing cumulative snapshot streams for the same output slot still render as a single updated text block instead of duplicate repeated text.

No configuration, migration, or operator action is required.

## Evidence

- `git diff --check` passed.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/ai/src/providers/openai-responses-shared.test.ts` passed: 1 file, 71 tests.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/openai-transport-stream.base.test.ts` passed: 1 file, 45 tests.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/openai-transport-stream.streaming.test.ts` passed: 1 file, 43 tests.
- Dependency contract checked locally: `node_modules/openai/resources/responses/responses.d.ts` declares `output_index: number` on both `ResponseOutputItemAddedEvent` and `ResponseOutputItemDoneEvent`.
- Attempted `node scripts/check-changed.mjs -- packages/ai/src/providers/openai-responses-stream-compat.ts packages/ai/src/providers/openai-responses-shared.ts src/agents/openai-responses-transport.ts packages/ai/src/providers/openai-responses-shared.test.ts src/agents/openai-transport-stream.base.test.ts`; the delegated validation backend failed sanity checks before project checks ran.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed:** Separate same-phase Responses message items keep distinct text blocks when they have distinct `output_index` values, while cumulative snapshots with rotating message ids on the same `output_index` still collapse.

**Environment tested:** Local Linux checkout, Node v22.22.0, existing dependency install.

**Steps run after the patch:** Invoked the actual patched `processResponsesStream` function from `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-responses-shared.ts` via `node --import tsx --no-warnings --input-type=module`, using representative Responses stream events for both distinct-prefix messages and same-output-slot cumulative snapshots.

**Evidence after fix:** Terminal output from the production function call:

```text
{
  "distinctPrefix": {
    "content": [
      {
        "type": "text",
        "text": "Hello",
        "textSignature": "{\"v\":1,\"id\":\"msg_1\",\"phase\":\"final_answer\"}"
      },
      {
        "type": "text",
        "text": "Hello world!",
        "textSignature": "{\"v\":1,\"id\":\"msg_2\",\"phase\":\"final_answer\"}"
      }
    ],
    "events": [
      "text_start:0",
      "text_end:0",
      "text_start:1",
      "text_end:1"
    ]
  },
  "cumulativeSnapshot": {
    "content": [
      {
        "type": "text",
        "text": "Hello world!",
        "textSignature": "{\"v\":1,\"id\":\"msg_snap_2\",\"phase\":\"final_answer\"}"
      }
    ],
    "events": [
      "text_start:0",
      "text_end:0",
      "text_end:0"
    ]
  }
}
```

**Observed result:** The distinct-prefix case used `output_index` 0 then 1 and produced two text blocks with separate start/end stream events. The cumulative snapshot case used rotating ids on `output_index` 0 and produced one final text block while keeping the cumulative update behavior on index 0.

**Not tested:** A live OpenAI Responses network stream with a real model was not exercised; the proof uses the production stream processor against representative Responses events.
